title: A Window's cross-origin isolated capability is always false while its Document is being created
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

A window environment settings object's [cross-origin isolated capability](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#set-up-a-window-environment-settings-object) requires its `Window`'s associated `Document` to be [allowed to use](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#allowed-to-use) the "`cross-origin-isolated`" feature, and "allowed to use" returns false when the `Document` is not fully active. A `Document` only becomes fully active once it is its navigable's active document, but two algorithms read the capability before then:

- [Create and initialize a `Document` object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#initialise-the-document-object), with #12890, coarsens the navigation start time of documents without a fetch controller (`about:srcdoc`, `javascript:` URLs, etc.) given the capability. This happens after the `Window`'s associated `Document` is set, but the capability is always false there.
- [Create a new browsing context and document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#creating-a-new-browsing-context) coarsens the initial `about:blank` `Document`'s navigation start time given the capability before the `Window`'s associated `Document` is even set.

As a result, these time origins are always coarsened as if the agent cluster were not cross-origin isolated. The state needed is available at both points: the agent cluster's cross-origin-isolation mode and the `Document`'s permissions policy. The capability could check the permissions policy directly ("is feature enabled in document for origin") instead of going through "allowed to use". "Create a new browsing context and document" could then read it after the `Window`'s associated `Document` is set.
